All five findings addressed, lint clean, full `cli` package tests pass.

## What changed (`cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go` + `trail_cmd_test.go`)

1. **Partial-failure path now tested** — added `TestApplyTrailUpdateReportsPartialFailureWhenBodyPatchFails`: a recorder that 200s the metadata PATCH and 500s the body PATCH, asserting the error reports `"metadata updated, but body update failed"` and that both PATCHes were attempted. That branch was previously never exercised.

2. **Dead `BodyChanged` branch removed** from `buildTrailUpdateRequest`. Since body is always a separate PATCH and the sole production caller never sets `BodyChanged`, the `req.Body = &inputs.Body` branch was unreachable. Updated the doc comment to state the builder never carries the body, and replaced `TestBuildTrailUpdateRequestCanClearBody` with `TestBuildTrailUpdateRequestNeverIncludesBody`, which asserts the body is excluded even when `BodyChanged` is set.

3. **Numberless-trail check moved before the form** — interactive mode now returns the `"has no number yet; cannot update"` error up front instead of after the user fills out the form (the body seed is keyed by number).

4. **Body-fetch failure decoupled from status/title edits** — instead of failing the whole update when the body can't be loaded, it now prints a warning, omits the Body field from the form (so it can't be accidentally clobbered), and keeps Status/Title editable. The fail-closed safety (never seed an empty body into an editable field) is preserved.

5. **Label emptiness check made consistent** — the `noFlags` check now uses `len(...) == 0` to match `trailUpdateHasChanges`, `metadataChanged`, and `buildTrailUpdateRequest`, instead of `== nil`.
